import unittest
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

from dispatch.captions.model import CaptionTrack, CaptionGroup, Word, StyleConfig, LayoutConfig, AnimationConfig
from dispatch.captions.exporter import export_to_ass


class TestTextCaptionSeparation(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.output_ass = Path(self.temp_dir.name) / "test.ass"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp_dir.cleanup()

    def test_normal_text_layer_exports_single_dialogue_without_word_cuts(self):
        track = CaptionTrack(
            groups=[
                CaptionGroup(
                    id="txt_1",
                    type="text",
                    start=1.0,
                    end=4.0,
                    words=[
                        Word(id="w1", text="Normal", start=1.0, end=2.5),
                        Word(id="w2", text="Text", start=2.5, end=4.0),
                    ],
                    style=StyleConfig(
                        primary_color="#38BDF8",
                        highlight_color="#FFE600",
                        highlight_enabled=False,
                    ),
                )
            ]
        )
        export_to_ass(track, self.output_ass)
        content = self.output_ass.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # Normal text should export ONE single dialogue event across the whole 1.00-4.00 range
        dialogue_lines = [l for l in content.splitlines() if l.startswith("Dialogue:")]
        self.assertEqual(len(dialogue_lines), 1)
        self.assertIn("NORMAL TEXT", dialogue_lines[0])
        # Color &H00F8BD38& is #38BDF8 in ASS BGR
        self.assertIn("&H00F8BD38&", dialogue_lines[0])
        # Caption highlight &H0000E6FF& (#FFE600) must NOT be present
        self.assertNotIn("&H0000E6FF&", dialogue_lines[0])

    def test_caption_with_highlight_enabled_exports_highlight_color(self):
        track = CaptionTrack(
            groups=[
                CaptionGroup(
                    id="cap_1",
                    type="caption",
                    start=1.0,
                    end=4.0,
                    words=[
                        Word(id="w1", text="Spoken", start=1.0, end=2.5),
                        Word(id="w2", text="Words", start=2.5, end=4.0),
                    ],
                    style=StyleConfig(
                        primary_color="#FFFFFF",
                        highlight_color="#FFE600",
                        highlight_enabled=True,
                    ),
                )
            ]
        )
        export_to_ass(track, self.output_ass)
        content = self.output_ass.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # Caption with highlighting enabled SHOULD contain highlight color &H0000E6FF& (#FFE600)
        self.assertIn("&H0000E6FF&", content)
        self.assertIn("SPOKEN", content)
        self.assertIn("WORDS", content)

    def test_caption_with_highlight_disabled_exports_uniform_static_colors(self):
        track = CaptionTrack(
            groups=[
                CaptionGroup(
                    id="cap_off",
                    type="caption",
                    start=1.0,
                    end=4.0,
                    words=[
                        Word(id="w1", text="Uniform", start=1.0, end=2.5),
                        Word(id="w2", text="Caption", start=2.5, end=4.0),
                    ],
                    style=StyleConfig(
                        primary_color="#FFFFFF",
                        highlight_color="#FFE600",
                        highlight_enabled=False,
                    ),
                )
            ]
        )
        export_to_ass(track, self.output_ass)
        content = self.output_ass.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # Caption with highlight_enabled=False should NOT contain highlight color &H0000E6FF&
        self.assertNotIn("&H0000E6FF&", content)
        self.assertIn("UNIFORM", content)
        self.assertIn("CAPTION", content)

    def test_simultaneous_caption_and_text_both_exported(self):
        track = CaptionTrack(
            groups=[
                CaptionGroup(
                    id="cap_sub",
                    type="caption",
                    start=0.0,
                    end=5.0,
                    words=[Word(id="w1", text="Subtitle", start=0.0, end=5.0)],
                    layout=LayoutConfig(position_y=0.8),
                ),
                CaptionGroup(
                    id="txt_brand",
                    type="text",
                    start=0.0,
                    end=10.0,
                    words=[Word(id="w2", text="Brand", start=0.0, end=10.0)],
                    layout=LayoutConfig(position_y=0.1),
                ),
            ]
        )
        export_to_ass(track, self.output_ass)
        content = self.output_ass.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # Both dialogue lines must be present in the ASS output
        dialogue_lines = [l for l in content.splitlines() if l.startswith("Dialogue:")]
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(dialogue_lines), 2)
        self.assertTrue(any("SUBTITLE" in l for l in dialogue_lines))
        self.assertTrue(any("BRAND" in l for l in dialogue_lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

FILE: tests\test_text_visibility_and_glow.py

"""Regression Test Suite for Dispatch Text Visibility, Glow Rendering, and Animation Model.
Verifies:
1. Glow ON: emits background Gaussian glow on Layer 0 and crisp text on Layer 1.
2. Glow OFF: emits single crisp Layer 0 line; no glow emitted.
3. Glow preserves independent outline stroke and drop shadow.
4. AnimationConfig round-trip serialization (In, Out, Loop, Active-Word).
5. Phrase-level vs word-level ASS glow rendering parity.
"""
import unittest
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from dispatch.captions.model import (
    CaptionTrack, CaptionGroup, Word, StyleConfig, LayoutConfig, AnimationConfig
)
from dispatch.captions.exporter import export_to_ass


class TestTextVisibilityAndGlow(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.ass_path = Path(self.temp_dir.name) / "test.ass"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp_dir.cleanup()

    def test_glow_on_emits_layer0_blur_and_layer1_text(self):
        """When glow_enabled is True, exporter must emit Layer 0 Gaussian blur and Layer 1 crisp foreground."""
        style = StyleConfig(
            font_family="Montserrat",
            font_size=44,
            primary_color="#FFFFFF",
            highlight_color="#FFE600",
            glow_enabled=True,
            glow_color="#00F0FF",
            glow_blur=16.0,
            outline_enabled=True,
            outline_color="#000000",
            outline_width=3.0,
            shadow_enabled=True,
            shadow_color="#111111",
            shadow_blur=6.0,
        )

        words = [
            Word(id="w1", text="NEON", start=1.0, end=1.5, is_exact=True),
            Word(id="w2", text="GLOW", start=1.5, end=2.0, is_exact=True),
        ]
        group = CaptionGroup(id="g1", start=1.0, end=2.0, words=words, style=style)
        track = CaptionTrack(
            id="trk1",
            clip_id="clip_glow",
            default_style=style,
            default_layout=LayoutConfig(),
            default_animation=AnimationConfig(type="pop"),
            groups=[group],
        )

        export_to_ass(track, self.ass_path)
        content = self.ass_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # Layer 0 must contain blur and glow color
        self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,", content)
        self.assertIn(r"\blur16", content)
        self.assertIn(r"\alpha&H35&", content)

        # Layer 1 must contain crisp foreground text
        self.assertIn("Dialogue: 1,", content)
        # Outline and shadow must be preserved
        self.assertIn(r"\bord3.0", content)
        self.assertIn(r"\shad", content)

    def test_glow_off_emits_no_glow_layer(self):
        """When glow_enabled is False, only standard Dialogue line is emitted without glow tags."""
        style = StyleConfig(
            font_family="Montserrat",
            font_size=44,
            primary_color="#FFFFFF",
            glow_enabled=False,
            outline_enabled=True,
            outline_color="#000000",
            outline_width=2.0,
            shadow_enabled=False,
        )

        words = [
            Word(id="w1", text="CLEAN", start=0.5, end=1.5, is_exact=True),
        ]
        group = CaptionGroup(id="g1", start=0.5, end=1.5, words=words, style=style)
        track = CaptionTrack(
            id="trk2",
            clip_id="clip_noglow",
            default_style=style,
            default_layout=LayoutConfig(),
            default_animation=AnimationConfig(),
            groups=[group],
        )

        export_to_ass(track, self.ass_path)
        content = self.ass_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # Must not contain Layer 1 or alpha&H35& glow tags
        self.assertNotIn("Dialogue: 1,", content)
        self.assertNotIn(r"\alpha&H35&", content)
        # Dialogue: 0 must exist
        self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,", content)
        self.assertIn("CLEAN", content)

    def test_phrase_level_glow_parity(self):
        """Phrase-only captions (timing_mode='phrase') render glow on Layer 0 and text on Layer 1."""
        style = StyleConfig(
            font_family="Impact",
            font_size=50,
            primary_color="#FFFF00",
            glow_enabled=True,
            glow_color="#FF0055",
            glow_blur=14.0,
        )

        words = [
            Word(id="w1", text="PHRASE", start=2.0, end=4.0, is_exact=False),
            Word(id="w2", text="ONLY", start=2.0, end=4.0, is_exact=False),
        ]
        group = CaptionGroup(
            id="g_phrase",
            start=2.0,
            end=4.0,
            words=words,
            style=style,
            timing_mode="phrase",
            has_word_timing=False,
        )
        track = CaptionTrack(
            id="trk3",
            clip_id="clip_phrase",
            default_style=style,
            default_layout=LayoutConfig(),
            default_animation=AnimationConfig(),
            groups=[group],
        )

        export_to_ass(track, self.ass_path)
        content = self.ass_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,0:00:02.00,0:00:04.00,Default,,0,0,0,", content)
        self.assertIn("Dialogue: 1,0:00:02.00,0:00:04.00,Default,,0,0,0,", content)
        self.assertIn(r"\blur14", content)
        self.assertIn("PHRASE ONLY", content)

    def test_animation_config_serialization(self):
        """AnimationConfig round-trip preserves in/out/loop/active_word configuration."""
        anim_data = {
            "type": "pop",
            "duration_ms": 120,
            "active_scale": 1.22,
            "enter": {"type": "slide_up", "duration_ms": 250},
            "exit": {"type": "fade", "duration_ms": 180},
            "loop": {"type": "pulse", "speed_ms": 900},
            "active_word": {"type": "pop", "active_scale": 1.25, "duration_ms": 110},
        }

        cfg = AnimationConfig.from_dict(anim_data)
        self.assertEqual(cfg.enter_type, "slide_up")
        self.assertEqual(cfg.enter_duration_ms, 250)
        self.assertEqual(cfg.exit_type, "fade")
        self.assertEqual(cfg.exit_duration_ms, 180)
        self.assertEqual(cfg.loop_type, "pulse")
        self.assertEqual(cfg.loop_speed_ms, 900)
        self.assertEqual(cfg.active_word.get("active_scale"), 1.25)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""tests/test_thumbnail_freshness.py
Comprehensive test suite verifying Dispatch video thumbnail freshness,
automatic regeneration, atomic generation, cache invalidation, sub-second
fingerprinting, concurrency serialization, and HTTP headers.
"""
import concurrent.futures
import os
import subprocess
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from dispatch.config import CLIPS_DIR
from dispatch import db
from dispatch.video_engine.thumbnail import (
    is_thumbnail_stale,
    generate_thumbnail_from_video,
    ensure_clip_thumbnail,
    get_file_fingerprint,
    get_thumbnail_version,
    get_thumbnail_version_token,
    populate_clip_media_urls,
)
from dispatch.web.app import app


class TestThumbnailFreshness(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        db.init_db()
        CLIPS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cls.test_video_path = CLIPS_DIR / "test_thumb_source.mp4"
        cls.test_video_alt_path = CLIPS_DIR / "test_thumb_source_alt.mp4"

        # Generate lightweight 2-second color videos via ffmpeg for deterministic testing
        cmd1 = [
            "ffmpeg", "-y",
            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "color=c=navy:s=320x240:d=2",
            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "anullsrc=channel_layout=stereo:sample_rate=44100",
            "-c:v", "libx264", "-t", "2",
            "-c:a", "aac", "-shortest",
            "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
            str(cls.test_video_path)
        ]
        res1 = subprocess.run(cmd1, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        if res1.returncode != 0 or not cls.test_video_path.exists():
            raise RuntimeError("Failed to generate test video fixture with ffmpeg")

        cmd2 = [
            "ffmpeg", "-y",
            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "color=c=crimson:s=320x240:d=2",
            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "anullsrc=channel_layout=stereo:sample_rate=44100",
            "-c:v", "libx264", "-t", "2",
            "-c:a", "aac", "-shortest",
            "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
            str(cls.test_video_alt_path)
        ]
        subprocess.run(cmd2, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        for p in (cls.test_video_path, cls.test_video_alt_path):
            if p.exists():
                try:
                    p.unlink()
                except Exception:
                    pass

    def test_01_is_thumbnail_stale_logic(self):
        """Test timestamp-based staleness logic across file existence and mtimes."""
        vpath = self.test_video_path
        tpath = CLIPS_DIR / "temp_logic_test.jpg"

        # Missing thumbnail is stale
        if tpath.exists():
            tpath.unlink()
        self.assertTrue(is_thumbnail_stale(vpath, tpath))

        # 0-byte thumbnail is stale
        tpath.touch()
        self.assertTrue(is_thumbnail_stale(vpath, tpath))

        # Non-empty thumbnail older than video is stale
        tpath.write_bytes(b"dummy image content for testing")
        vid_mtime = vpath.stat().st_mtime
        os.utime(str(tpath), (vid_mtime - 10.0, vid_mtime - 10.0))
        self.assertTrue(is_thumbnail_stale(vpath, tpath))

        # Non-empty thumbnail newer than or equal to video is fresh
        os.utime(str(tpath), (vid_mtime + 5.0, vid_mtime + 5.0))
        self.assertFalse(is_thumbnail_stale(vpath, tpath))

        # Clean up
        if tpath.exists():
            tpath.unlink()

    def test_02_atomic_generation_and_no_leftover_temps(self):
        """Test that FFmpeg extracts frame atomically and leaves no temporary files."""
        out_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / "test_atomic_thumb.jpg"
        meta_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / "test_atomic_thumb.jpg.meta"
        for p in (out_thumb, meta_thumb):
            if p.exists():
                p.unlink()

        success = generate_thumbnail_from_video(self.test_video_path, out_thumb, timestamp_sec=0.5)
        self.assertTrue(success)
        self.assertTrue(out_thumb.exists())
        self.assertGreater(out_thumb.stat().st_size, 100)
        self.assertTrue(meta_thumb.exists(), "Sidecar metadata must be created atomically alongside thumbnail")

        # Verify no .tmp_* files remain in CLIPS_DIR
        temp_files = list(CLIPS_DIR.glob(".tmp_*test_atomic_thumb*"))
        self.assertEqual(len(temp_files), 0, "No temporary thumbnail files should remain after generation")

        # Clean up
        out_thumb.unlink()
        if meta_thumb.exists():
            meta_thumb.unlink()

    def test_03_video_replacement_triggers_thumbnail_regeneration(self):
        """When a video is updated/replaced with same clip ID, ensure_clip_thumbnail regenerates it."""
        clip_id = db.save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.0,
            end_time=2.0,
            title="Replacement Test Clip",
            hook="Hook",
            description="Desc",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=80,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )
        clip_vid = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.mp4"
        clip_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg"
        clip_meta = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg.meta"

        # Copy test video to clip_vid
        clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_path.read_bytes())
        t0 = time.time() - 20.0
        os.utime(str(clip_vid), (t0, t0))

        db.update_clip_media(clip_id=clip_id, video_path=str(clip_vid), thumbnail_path=str(clip_thumb))

        # 1. Initial generation
        first_path = ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)
        self.assertIsNotNone(first_path)
        self.assertTrue(clip_thumb.exists())
        initial_thumb_mtime = clip_thumb.stat().st_mtime

        # 2. Simulate video file replacement on PC (newer mtime)
        t_new = initial_thumb_mtime + 10.0
        os.utime(str(clip_vid), (t_new, t_new))
        self.assertTrue(is_thumbnail_stale(clip_vid, clip_thumb))

        # 3. Call ensure_clip_thumbnail: must detect staleness and regenerate!
        second_path = ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)
        self.assertIsNotNone(second_path)
        new_thumb_mtime = clip_thumb.stat().st_mtime

        self.assertGreater(new_thumb_mtime, initial_thumb_mtime,
                           "Thumbnail modification time must increase after video replacement")
        self.assertFalse(is_thumbnail_stale(clip_vid, clip_thumb),
                         "Regenerated thumbnail must be recognized as fresh")

        # Clean up
        clip_vid.unlink()
        clip_thumb.unlink()
        if clip_meta.exists():
            clip_meta.unlink()

    def test_04_unchanged_video_skips_unnecessary_regeneration(self):
        """Unchanged videos must preserve their cached thumbnail without re-invoking FFmpeg."""
        clip_id = db.save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.0,
            end_time=2.0,
            title="Cache Hit Test Clip",
            hook="Hook",
            description="Desc",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=80,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )
        clip_vid = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.mp4"
        clip_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg"
        clip_meta = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg.meta"

        clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_path.read_bytes())
        db.update_clip_media(clip_id=clip_id, video_path=str(clip_vid), thumbnail_path=str(clip_thumb))

        # First run generates thumbnail
        ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)
        self.assertTrue(clip_thumb.exists())
        first_mtime = clip_thumb.stat().st_mtime

        # Second run on unchanged video must be a cache hit (same mtime)
        ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)
        second_mtime = clip_thumb.stat().st_mtime
        self.assertEqual(first_mtime, second_mtime, "Thumbnail must not be modified when video is unchanged")

        # Clean up
        clip_vid.unlink()
        clip_thumb.unlink()
        if clip_meta.exists():
            clip_meta.unlink()

    def test_05_populate_clip_media_urls_version_query_strings(self):
        """populate_clip_media_urls must inject robust ?v={token} into URLs for cache invalidation."""
        clip_id = db.save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.0,
            end_time=2.0,
            title="Populate URLs Test",
            hook="Hook",
            description="Desc",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=80,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )
        clip_vid = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.mp4"
        clip_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg"
        clip_meta = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg.meta"

        clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_path.read_bytes())
        db.update_clip_media(clip_id=clip_id, video_path=str(clip_vid), thumbnail_path=str(clip_thumb))

        clip_dict = db.get_clip_by_id(clip_id)
        populated = populate_clip_media_urls(clip_dict)

        self.assertIn("thumbnail_url", populated)
        self.assertIn("video_url", populated)
        self.assertIn("source_video_url", populated)

        # Check that robust version token is present
        self.assertRegex(populated["thumbnail_url"], r"^/clips/.*\.jpg\?v=[\w\d_-]+$")
        self.assertRegex(populated["video_url"], r"^/clips/.*\.mp4\?v=\d+$")

        # Version matches deterministic version token
        expected_token = get_thumbnail_version_token(clip_thumb)
        self.assertEqual(populated["thumbnail_url"], f"/clips/{clip_thumb.name}?v={expected_token}")
        self.assertEqual(populated["thumbnail_version"], expected_token)

        # Clean up
        clip_vid.unlink()
        clip_thumb.unlink()
        if clip_meta.exists():
            clip_meta.unlink()

    def test_06_http_cache_headers_and_conditional_revalidation(self):
        """Verify RFC 9111 HTTP cache headers: max-age on versioned, no-cache on unversioned, and 304."""
        clip_id = db.save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.0,
            end_time=2.0,
            title="HTTP Headers Test",
            hook="Hook",
            description="Desc",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=80,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )
        clip_vid = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.mp4"
        clip_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg"
        clip_meta = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg.meta"

        clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_path.read_bytes())
        db.update_clip_media(clip_id=clip_id, video_path=str(clip_vid), thumbnail_path=str(clip_thumb))

        ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)
        self.assertTrue(clip_thumb.exists())
        thumb_v = get_thumbnail_version_token(clip_thumb)

        client = TestClient(app)

        # 1. Versioned request (?v=...) -> public, max-age=86400
        res_v = client.get(f"/clips/{clip_thumb.name}?v={thumb_v}")
        self.assertEqual(res_v.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("public", res_v.headers.get("cache-control", ""))
        self.assertIn("max-age=86400", res_v.headers.get("cache-control", ""))
        etag = res_v.headers.get("etag")
        self.assertIsNotNone(etag)

        # 2. Unversioned request -> no-cache, must-revalidate
        res_unv = client.get(f"/clips/{clip_thumb.name}")
        self.assertEqual(res_unv.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("no-cache", res_unv.headers.get("cache-control", ""))

        # 3. Conditional GET with If-None-Match -> 304 Not Modified
        res_cond = client.get(f"/clips/{clip_thumb.name}", headers={"If-None-Match": etag})
        self.assertEqual(res_cond.status_code, 304)

        # Clean up
        clip_vid.unlink()
        clip_thumb.unlink()
        if clip_meta.exists():
            clip_meta.unlink()

    def test_08_filmstrip_freshness_detection_and_regeneration(self):
        """Filmstrip frames must regenerate and return fresh ?v= parameters when video changes."""
        clip_id = db.save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.0,
            end_time=2.0,
            title="Filmstrip Freshness Test",
            hook="Hook",
            description="Desc",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=80,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )
        clip_vid = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.mp4"

        clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_path.read_bytes())
        t0 = time.time() - 30.0
        os.utime(str(clip_vid), (t0, t0))

        clip_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg"
        clip_meta = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg.meta"
        db.update_clip_media(clip_id=clip_id, video_path=str(clip_vid), thumbnail_path=str(clip_thumb))

        client = TestClient(app)

        # 1. Fetch filmstrip for the first time
        res1 = client.get(f"/api/clips/{clip_id}/filmstrip")
        self.assertEqual(res1.status_code, 200)
        frames1 = res1.json().get("frames", [])
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(frames1), 1)
        self.assertIn("?v=", frames1[0])

        # 2. Modify video to newer timestamp
        t_mod = time.time() + 10.0
        os.utime(str(clip_vid), (t_mod, t_mod))

        # 3. Fetch filmstrip again: should detect stale frames and re-extract with updated ?v=
        res2 = client.get(f"/api/clips/{clip_id}/filmstrip")
        self.assertEqual(res2.status_code, 200)
        frames2 = res2.json().get("frames", [])
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(frames2), 1)

        # Clean up frames
        for i in range(12):
            for ext in (".jpg", ".jpg.meta"):
                fpath = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}_frame_{i}{ext}"
                if fpath.exists():
                    try:
                        fpath.unlink()
                    except Exception:
                        pass
        clip_vid.unlink()
        if clip_thumb.exists():
            clip_thumb.unlink()
        if clip_meta.exists():
            clip_meta.unlink()

    def test_09_same_second_replacement_and_preserved_timestamp_detection(self):
        """Verify that fingerprinting and nanoseconds detect replacements even with identical integer timestamps."""
        clip_id = db.save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.0,
            end_time=2.0,
            title="Fingerprint Staleness Test",
            hook="Hook",
            description="Desc",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=85,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )
        clip_vid = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.mp4"
        clip_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg"
        clip_meta = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg.meta"

        # 1. Initial write of navy video
        clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_path.read_bytes())
        fixed_t = 1700000000.0  # Stable integer timestamp
        os.utime(str(clip_vid), (fixed_t, fixed_t))
        db.update_clip_media(clip_id=clip_id, video_path=str(clip_vid), thumbnail_path=str(clip_thumb))

        # Generate thumbnail
        ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)
        self.assertTrue(clip_thumb.exists())
        self.assertFalse(is_thumbnail_stale(clip_vid, clip_thumb))
        initial_token = get_thumbnail_version_token(clip_thumb)

        # 2. Replace with crimson video BUT preserve the exact same integer timestamp fixed_t
        if self.test_video_alt_path.exists():
            clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_alt_path.read_bytes())
            os.utime(str(clip_vid), (fixed_t, fixed_t))

            # Fingerprint must detect that content changed even though mtime didn't increase!
            self.assertTrue(
                is_thumbnail_stale(clip_vid, clip_thumb),
                "Content fingerprint must detect replacement even when timestamp is preserved"
            )

            # Regenerate thumbnail
            ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)
            new_token = get_thumbnail_version_token(clip_thumb)
            self.assertNotEqual(initial_token, new_token, "Version token must change when content changes")
            self.assertFalse(is_thumbnail_stale(clip_vid, clip_thumb))

        # Clean up
        clip_vid.unlink()
        clip_thumb.unlink()
        if clip_meta.exists():
            clip_meta.unlink()

    def test_10_concurrent_thumbnail_requests_serialize_safely(self):
        """Concurrent calls to ensure_clip_thumbnail for the same clip must not crash or race."""
        clip_id = db.save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.0,
            end_time=2.0,
            title="Concurrency Test",
            hook="Hook",
            description="Desc",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=80,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )
        clip_vid = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.mp4"
        clip_thumb = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg"
        clip_meta = CLIPS_DIR / f"{clip_id}.jpg.meta"

        clip_vid.write_bytes(self.test_video_path.read_bytes())
        db.update_clip_media(clip_id=clip_id, video_path=str(clip_vid), thumbnail_path=str(clip_thumb))

        def _worker():
            return ensure_clip_thumbnail(clip_id)

        # Execute 6 parallel requests across threads
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as executor:
            futures = [executor.submit(_worker) for _ in range(6)]
            results = [f.result() for f in futures]

        for res in results:
            self.assertIsNotNone(res)
            self.assertEqual(res, clip_thumb)

        self.assertTrue(clip_thumb.exists())
        self.assertGreater(clip_thumb.stat().st_size, 100)

        # Ensure no dangling temporary files
        temp_files = list(CLIPS_DIR.glob(f".tmp_*{clip_id}*"))
        self.assertEqual(len(temp_files), 0, "No orphaned temporary files should remain after concurrent runs")

        # Clean up
        clip_vid.unlink()
        clip_thumb.unlink()
        if clip_meta.exists():
            clip_meta.unlink()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Vault round-trip (Worker-compatible AES-GCM format) and remote-job claim/finish
semantics with mocked Supabase RPCs."""

import base64
import os
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

from dispatch import youtube_connections as yc


def b64url(bytes_: bytes) -> str:
    import base64 as b
    return b.urlsafe_b64encode(bytes_).decode().rstrip("=")


class TestVaultRoundTrip(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.key = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode()
        self._env = patch.dict(os.environ, {"DISPATCH_TOKEN_VAULT_KEY": self.key})
        self._env.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._env.stop)

    def _encrypt_like_worker(self, plaintext: str) -> str:
        iv = os.urandom(12)
        ct = AESGCM(base64.b64decode(self.key)).encrypt(iv, plaintext.encode(), None)
        return b64url(iv + ct)

    def test_worker_encrypted_token_decrypts_on_pc(self):
        token = "1//0gRefreshTokenFromGoogle"
        enc = self._encrypt_like_worker(token)
        self.assertEqual(yc.decrypt_refresh_token(enc), token)

    def test_tampered_ciphertext_fails_closed(self):
        # Deterministic corruption: flip one ciphertext byte in the middle - the GCM
        # tag MUST reject it. (Base64-tail edits can decode to identical bytes: flaky.)
        import base64 as b64
        enc = self._encrypt_like_worker("secret")
        raw = bytearray(b64.urlsafe_b64decode(enc + "=" * (-len(enc) % 4)))
        raw[len(raw) // 2] ^= 0x01
        tampered = b64url(bytes(raw))
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            yc.decrypt_refresh_token(tampered)


    def test_missing_vault_key_raises_unavailable(self):
        os.environ.pop("DISPATCH_TOKEN_VAULT_KEY", None)
        with self.assertRaises(yc.VaultUnavailable):
            yc.vault_key()




class TestRemoteJobs(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_claim_returns_job_and_finish_records_status(self):
        calls = []

        def fake_rpc(action, params):
            calls.append((action, params))
            if action == "cloud_claim_job":
                return [{"job_id": "j1", "user_id": "u1", "youtube_url": "https://youtu.be/x"}]
            return None

        with patch.object(yc, "_supabase_rpc", side_effect=fake_rpc):
            job = yc.claim_remote_job("owner-pc-1")
            self.assertEqual(job.job_id, "j1")
            yc.finish_remote_job("j1", "done", "vid", "")

        self.assertEqual(calls[1][0], "cloud_finish_job")

    def test_empty_queue_returns_none(self):
        with patch.object(yc, "_supabase_rpc", return_value=[]):
            self.assertIsNone(yc.claim_remote_job("w"))

    def test_poller_processes_claimed_job_through_ingest(self):
        processed = []
        with patch.object(yc, "_supabase_rpc", return_value=[]), \
             patch.object(yc, "claim_remote_job", return_value=yc.RemoteJob("j9", "u9", "https://youtu.be/ok")):
            poller = yc.RemoteJobPoller(ingest_video=lambda url: processed.append(url) or {"status": "DOWNLOADED", "video_id": "v9"})
            poller._process(poller and yc.claim_remote_job("w"))
        self.assertEqual(processed, ["https://youtu.be/ok"])

    def test_ingest_failure_marks_job_failed(self):
        with patch.object(yc, "_supabase_rpc", return_value=[]) as rpc, \
             patch.object(yc, "claim_remote_job", return_value=yc.RemoteJob("j8", "u8", "https://youtu.be/bad")):
            poller = yc.RemoteJobPoller(ingest_video=lambda url: {"status": "FAILED", "error": "private"})
            poller._process(yc.claim_remote_job("w"))
        finish_calls = [c for c in rpc.call_args_list if c.args[0] == "cloud_finish_job"]
        self.assertEqual(finish_calls[0].args[1]["p_status"], "failed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Unit test for Phase 6: Remote Connectivity & Transport Abstraction."""
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock

from dispatch.transport.transport_manager import (
    TransportManager,
    EndpointCandidate,
    NetworkPolicy
)


class TestTransportManager(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.auth_token = "secret_paired_token_123"
        self.manager = TransportManager(
            auth_token=self.auth_token,
            lan_url="http://192.168.1.50:8765",
            tailscale_url="http://laptop.tailscale.net:8765"
        )

    def test_auth_headers(self):
        headers = self.manager.get_auth_headers()
        self.assertEqual(headers["X-Dispatch-Device-Token"], self.auth_token)
        self.assertIn("X-Dispatch-Client", headers)

    def test_network_policy_evaluation(self):
        # 1. Disconnected
        allowed, reason = self.manager.evaluate_network_policy("none")
        self.assertFalse(allowed)

        # 2. Wi-Fi allowed
        allowed, reason = self.manager.evaluate_network_policy("wifi")
        self.assertTrue(allowed)

        # 3. Roaming blocked
        allowed, reason = self.manager.evaluate_network_policy("wifi", is_roaming=True)
        self.assertFalse(allowed)
        self.assertIn("roaming", reason.lower())

        # 4. Cellular disallowed by default
        allowed, reason = self.manager.evaluate_network_policy("cellular")
        self.assertFalse(allowed)
        self.assertIn("cellular sync is disabled", reason.lower())

        # 5. Cellular allowed if policy enables it
        manager_cell = TransportManager(
            auth_token=self.auth_token,
            policy=NetworkPolicy(allow_cellular=True, wifi_only=False)
        )
        allowed, reason = manager_cell.evaluate_network_policy("cellular")
        self.assertTrue(allowed)

    def test_route_probing_and_failover(self):
        # Case 1: Both LAN and Tailscale online -> LAN preferred (priority 1)
        def mock_requests_get(url, **kwargs):
            mock_resp = MagicMock()
            mock_resp.status_code = 200
            mock_resp.json.return_value = {"status": "online"}
            return mock_resp

        with patch("requests.get", side_effect=mock_requests_get):
            best = self.manager.select_best_endpoint()
            self.assertIsNotNone(best)
            self.assertEqual(best.name, "lan")
            self.assertEqual(best.url, "http://192.168.1.50:8765")

        # Case 2: LAN offline, Tailscale online -> Auto failover to Tailscale
        def mock_lan_down_get(url, **kwargs):
            if "192.168" in url:
                raise ConnectionError("Host unreachable on local LAN")
            mock_resp = MagicMock()
            mock_resp.status_code = 200
            mock_resp.json.return_value = {"status": "online"}
            return mock_resp

        with patch("requests.get", side_effect=mock_lan_down_get):
            best = self.manager.select_best_endpoint()
            self.assertIsNotNone(best)
            self.assertEqual(best.name, "tailscale")
            self.assertEqual(best.url, "http://laptop.tailscale.net:8765")

        # Case 3: Both offline -> None returned (safe queue in phone outbox)
        with patch("requests.get", side_effect=ConnectionError("All networks down")):
            best = self.manager.select_best_endpoint()
            self.assertIsNone(best)


from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from dispatch.web.app import app
from dispatch.sync.receiver import (
    get_auth_token,
    get_pairing_pin,
    _FAILED_PIN_ATTEMPTS,
    _PIN_LOCKOUTS,
)
from dispatch.transport.discovery import (
    DiscoveryBeaconServer,
    BEACON_MAGIC,
    SERVICE_VERSION,
)


class TestDiscoveryAndPairingSecurity(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # Client simulating a remote phone / LAN device
        self.lan_client = TestClient(app, client=("192.168.1.100", 50000))
        # Client simulating laptop localhost
        self.local_client = TestClient(app, client=("127.0.0.1", 50000))
        self.expected_token = get_auth_token()
        self.expected_pin = get_pairing_pin()
        _FAILED_PIN_ATTEMPTS.clear()
        _PIN_LOCKOUTS.clear()

    def test_udp_discovery_beacon_does_not_leak_auth_token(self):
        """Milestone 1 Acceptance: UDP discovery beacon must NOT broadcast master auth token."""
        server = DiscoveryBeaconServer()
        payload = server._get_payload()
        self.assertEqual(payload["magic"], BEACON_MAGIC)
        self.assertEqual(payload["service"], "dispatch")
        self.assertEqual(payload["version"], SERVICE_VERSION)
        self.assertTrue(payload.get("pairing_required"))
        self.assertIn("lan_url", payload)
        self.assertIn("ip", payload)
        self.assertIn("port", payload)
        self.assertIn("hostname", payload)
        # CRITICAL: auth_token must NOT be present in LAN UDP broadcast
        self.assertNotIn("auth_token", payload, "UDP discovery beacon must not leak auth_token to LAN sniffers")
        self.assertNotIn("token", payload)
        self.assertNotIn(self.expected_token, str(payload))

    def test_pairing_config_unauthenticated_lan_request_rejected(self):
        """Milestone 1 Acceptance: Unauthenticated LAN requests return 401 without tokens."""
        resp = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 401)
        self.assertIn("WWW-Authenticate", resp.headers)
        resp_data = resp.json()

        # Absolute guarantee: no secrets in payload
        self.assertNotIn("auth_token", resp_data)
        self.assertNotIn("connection_string", resp_data)
        self.assertNotIn("yt_token", resp_data)
        self.assertNotIn("yt_refresh", resp_data)
        self.assertNotIn("yt_client_id", resp_data)
        self.assertNotIn("yt_client_secret", resp_data)
        self.assertNotIn(self.expected_token, resp.text)

    def test_pairing_config_masked_discovery_returns_200_without_secrets(self):
        """Masked discovery mode returns 200 OK with null secrets for safe network probing."""
        resp = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config?mask=true")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        data = resp.json()
        self.assertIsNone(data["auth_token"])
        self.assertIsNone(data["pairing_pin"])
        self.assertIsNone(data["connection_string"])
        self.assertIsNone(data["yt_token"])
        self.assertFalse(data["authenticated"])
        self.assertTrue(data["requires_pairing"])
        self.assertIn("lan_url", data)

    def test_pairing_config_localhost_exemption_for_web_dashboard(self):
        """Localhost web dashboard is exempt and receives pairing credentials."""
        resp = self.local_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        data = resp.json()
        self.assertEqual(data["auth_token"], self.expected_token)
        self.assertEqual(data["pairing_pin"], self.expected_pin)
        self.assertTrue(data["authenticated"])
        self.assertIn("lan_url", data)
        self.assertIn("connection_string", data)

    def test_pairing_config_invalid_pin_or_token_rejected_with_401(self):
        """Invalid PIN or invalid token from LAN must be rejected with 401."""
        # Wrong PIN via header
        resp_bad_pin = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config", headers={"x-pairing-pin": "000000"})
        self.assertEqual(resp_bad_pin.status_code, 401)
        self.assertIn("Invalid pairing PIN", resp_bad_pin.text)
        self.assertIn("WWW-Authenticate", resp_bad_pin.headers)

        # Wrong PIN via query param
        resp_bad_pin_q = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config?pin=000000")
        self.assertEqual(resp_bad_pin_q.status_code, 401)

        # Wrong Auth Token
        resp_bad_tok = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config", headers={"x-auth-token": "bad_token_123"})
        self.assertEqual(resp_bad_tok.status_code, 401)
        self.assertIn("Invalid authentication token", resp_bad_tok.text)

    def test_pairing_config_authenticated_with_pin(self):
        """Client providing valid 6-digit pairing PIN successfully authenticates and receives tokens."""
        # Query parameter
        resp_query = self.lan_client.get(f"/api/sync/pairing/config?pin={self.expected_pin}")
        self.assertEqual(resp_query.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp_query.json()["auth_token"], self.expected_token)
        self.assertIn("lan_url", resp_query.json())
        self.assertTrue(resp_query.json()["authenticated"])

        # Header parameter
        resp_hdr = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config", headers={"x-pairing-pin": self.expected_pin})
        self.assertEqual(resp_hdr.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp_hdr.json()["auth_token"], self.expected_token)

    def test_pairing_config_authenticated_with_device_token(self):
        """Previously paired client providing x-auth-token successfully retrieves current config."""
        resp = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config", headers={"x-auth-token": self.expected_token})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.json()["auth_token"], self.expected_token)

    def test_pin_brute_force_lockout_returns_429(self):
        """Brute-force protection: 5 failed PIN attempts results in 300s lockout returning 429."""
        ip = "192.168.1.222"
        attacker_client = TestClient(app, client=(ip, 50000))

        # First 5 attempts return 401
        for i in range(5):
            res = attacker_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config?pin=000000")
            self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 401)

        # 6th attempt must be locked out with 429 Too Many Requests
        res_lockout = attacker_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config?pin=000000")
        self.assertEqual(res_lockout.status_code, 429)
        self.assertIn("Too many failed pairing attempts", res_lockout.text)

        # Even if attacker now supplies correct PIN, they remain locked out
        res_locked_valid = attacker_client.get(f"/api/sync/pairing/config?pin={self.expected_pin}")
        self.assertEqual(res_locked_valid.status_code, 429)

    def test_pairing_handshake_endpoint(self):
        """Explicit POST /api/sync/pairing/handshake endpoint."""
        # Failure with wrong PIN
        res_fail = self.lan_client.post("/api/sync/pairing/handshake", json={"pin": "wrong_pin", "client_name": "POCO C65"})
        self.assertEqual(res_fail.status_code, 401)
        self.assertIn("Invalid pairing PIN", res_fail.text)

        # Success with valid PIN
        res_ok = self.lan_client.post("/api/sync/pairing/handshake", json={"pin": self.expected_pin, "client_name": "POCO C65"})
        self.assertEqual(res_ok.status_code, 200)
        data = res_ok.json()
        self.assertEqual(data["status"], "paired")
        self.assertEqual(data["auth_token"], self.expected_token)
        self.assertIn("lan_url", data)
        self.assertIn("connection_string", data)

    def test_simulated_android_discovery_and_handshake_flow(self):
        """Simulate complete Android discovery & pairing flow."""
        server = DiscoveryBeaconServer()
        payload = server._get_payload()
        discovered_ip = payload["ip"]
        discovered_port = payload["port"]
        discovered_url = payload["lan_url"]
        self.assertTrue(discovered_ip and discovered_port)
        self.assertTrue(payload.get("pairing_required"))

        # Step 1: Android tests reachability on ping endpoint
        ping_resp = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/ping")
        self.assertEqual(ping_resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(ping_resp.json()["status"], "online")

        # Step 2: Unauthenticated probe fails with 401 (no leak)
        unauth_resp = self.lan_client.get("/api/sync/pairing/config")
        self.assertEqual(unauth_resp.status_code, 401)
        self.assertNotIn("auth_token", unauth_resp.text)

        # Step 3: Phone submits pairing PIN entered by user
        pair_resp = self.lan_client.post("/api/sync/pairing/handshake", json={
            "pin": self.expected_pin,
            "client_name": "POCO C65"
        })
        self.assertEqual(pair_resp.status_code, 200)
        acquired_token = pair_resp.json()["auth_token"]
        self.assertEqual(acquired_token, self.expected_token)

        # Step 4: Phone can now perform authenticated operations
        auth_check = self.lan_client.get(
            "/api/sync/verify-chunk?segment_id=dummy&sha256=none",
            headers={"x-auth-token": acquired_token}
        )
        self.assertEqual(auth_check.status_code, 200)
        self.assertFalse(auth_check.json()["verified"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "sine=frequency=440",
            "-t", "7",
            "-c:v", "libx264",
            "-c:a", "aac",
            str(test_src)
        ]
        subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True)

        mock_segments = [
            {
                "id": 0, "start": 0.5, "end": 5.5,

                    {"word": "Yeh", "start": 0.5, "end": 0.8},
                    {"word": "Dispatch", "start": 0.9, "end": 1.4},
                    {"word": "automation", "start": 1.5, "end": 2.0},
                    {"word": "test", "start": 2.1, "end": 2.4},
                    {"word": "hai", "start": 2.5, "end": 3.0},
                ]
            }
        ]

            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=0.5,
            end_time=6.0,

            hook="Opening test",
            description="Description",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=88,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )

        # 3. Render clip

            source_video=test_src,
            clip_id=clip_id,
            start_time=0.5,
            end_time=6.0,
            aspect_ratio="16:9",
            layout_mode="fit_blur",
            segments=mock_segments
        )

        out_video = render_result["video_path"]
        out_thumb = render_result["thumbnail_path"]

        self.assertTrue(out_video.exists(), f"Rendered video does not exist: {out_video}")
        self.assertTrue(out_thumb.exists(), f"Thumbnail does not exist: {out_thumb}")

        # 4. Probe rendered vertical video
        valid, meta, err = probe_video(out_video)
        self.assertTrue(valid, f"Rendered video is invalid: {err}")
        self.assertEqual(meta["width"], 1080, f"Expected width 1080, got {meta['width']}")
        self.assertEqual(meta["height"], 1920, f"Expected height 1920, got {meta['height']}")
        self.assertEqual(meta["aspect_ratio"], "9:16", f"Expected 9:16, got {meta['aspect_ratio']}")

        # Clean up test artifacts
        test_src.unlink()
        out_video.unlink()
        out_thumb.unlink()

    def test_final_caption_export_failure_stops_render(self):
        from dispatch.captions import CaptionTrack

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            source = Path(directory) / "source.mp4"
            source.write_bytes(b"source")
            track = CaptionTrack(clip_id="caption_export_failure")

            with patch("dispatch.ingestion.validator.inspect_video_orientation", return_value={
                "valid": True,
                "orientation": "landscape",
                "has_audio": True,
            }), patch("dispatch.captions.exporter.export_to_ass", side_effect=OSError("disk full")), \
                 patch("dispatch.video_engine.renderer.subprocess.run") as ffmpeg:
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "Final caption export failed"):
                    render_clip(
                        source_video=source,
                        clip_id="caption_export_failure",
                        start_time=0,
                        end_time=10,
                        layout_mode="fit_blur",
                        subtitle_options={
                            "enabled": True,
                            "caption_track": track.to_dict(),
                            "preserve_timing": True,
                        },
                    )

            ffmpeg.assert_not_called()

import unittest
import tempfile

from unittest.mock import patch
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from dispatch.web.app import app
from dispatch.db import init_db, save_clip, update_clip_media

client = TestClient(app)

class TestWebDashboard(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_web_dashboard(self):
        init_db()

        # 1. Test homepage
        res = client.get("/")
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200, f"Expected 200, got {res.status_code}")
        self.assertIn("Dispatch", res.text)

        # 2. Test status endpoint
        res = client.get("/api/status")
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200)
        data = res.json()
        self.assertIn("disk_free_gb", data)
        self.assertIn("ready_clips", data)

        # 3. Create a test clip and verify list endpoint
        clip_id = save_clip(
            session_id=None,
            chunk_id=None,
            start_time=1.0,
            end_time=25.0,
            title="Web test clip title",
            hook="Opening test",
            description="Description",
            hashtags="#Test",
            virality_score=85,
            layout_mode="fit_blur"
        )

        res = client.get("/api/clips")
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200)
        clips_data = res.json()
        clip_ids = [c["id"] for c in clips_data["ready"]]
        self.assertIn(clip_id, clip_ids, f"Clip {clip_id} not found in ready list")

        # 4. Test approval
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            source = Path(tmp) / "source.mp4"
            output = Path(tmp) / "rendered.mp4"
            source.write_bytes(b"test source")

            def render_for_test(**kwargs):
                output.write_bytes(b"test rendered media")
                update_clip_media(kwargs["clip_id"], str(output), None, kwargs["layout_mode"])
                return {"video_path": str(output)}

            with patch("dispatch.web.app.resolve_clip_source_path", return_value=source), \
                 patch("dispatch.web.app.render_clip", side_effect=render_for_test), \
                 patch("dispatch.ingestion.validator.probe_video", return_value=(True, {"duration": 24.0}, None)):
                res = client.post(f"/api/clips/{clip_id}/approve", json={
                    "title": "Approved Title",
                    "hashtags": "#Approved",
                    "publish_mode": "private",
                    "platforms": "youtube,instagram"
                })
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(res.json()["status"], "success")

        # 5. Test pipeline jobs endpoint
        res = client.get("/api/pipeline/jobs")
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("jobs", res.json())

        # 6. Test integrations status endpoint
        res = client.get("/api/integrations/status")
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("youtube", res.json())

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from dispatch.sync.pairing_codes import (
    PairingCodeError,
    consume_pairing_code,
    issue_pairing_code,
    reset_pairing_codes_for_tests,
)
from scripts import auth_youtube


class YouTubeAuthTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
        self.root = Path(self.temp_dir.name)
        (self.root / "client_secrets.json").write_text("{}", encoding="utf-8")
        self.token_file = self.root / "youtube_token.json"
        self.token_file.write_text("old-token", encoding="utf-8")
        self.credentials = MagicMock(refresh_token="refresh", to_json=lambda: '{"token":"new"}')
        self.flow = MagicMock()
        self.flow.run_local_server.return_value = self.credentials

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp_dir.cleanup()

    def _run_auth(self, channels_result):
        service = MagicMock()
        service.channels.return_value.list.return_value.execute.return_value = channels_result
        with patch.object(auth_youtube, "ROOT_DIR", self.root), \
             patch.object(auth_youtube, "CLIENT_SECRETS_FILE", self.root / "client_secrets.json"), \
             patch.object(auth_youtube, "TOKEN_FILE", self.token_file), \
             patch("google_auth_oauthlib.flow.InstalledAppFlow.from_client_secrets_file", return_value=self.flow), \
             patch("googleapiclient.discovery.build", return_value=service):
            return auth_youtube.run_authentication()

    def test_token_is_saved_only_after_channel_verification(self):
        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
            self._run_auth({"items": []})
        self.assertEqual(self.token_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "old-token")

        channel = self._run_auth({"items": [{"id": "channel-id", "snippet": {"title": "Channel"}}]})
        self.assertEqual(channel["channel_id"], "channel-id")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.token_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), {"token": "new"})


class PairingCodeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        reset_pairing_codes_for_tests()

    def tearDown(self):
        reset_pairing_codes_for_tests()

    def test_generated_code_is_strictly_four_numeric_digits(self):
        """Verify that every generated code contains exactly four numeric digits."""
        for _ in range(50):
            code, expiry = issue_pairing_code()
            self.assertEqual(len(code), 4, f"Generated code {code} is not 4 digits")
            self.assertTrue(code.isdigit(), f"Generated code {code} is not all digits")
            self.assertEqual(expiry, 300)

    def test_code_with_leading_zeros_accepted(self):
        """Verify codes with leading zeros, such as '0047', are properly accepted."""
        with patch("secrets.randbelow", return_value=47):
            code, _ = issue_pairing_code()
            self.assertEqual(code, "0047")
            # Should consume without error
            consume_pairing_code("0047", "192.168.1.50")

    def test_invalid_length_and_non_numeric_codes_rejected(self):
        """Reject 3-digit, 5-digit, and non-numeric codes."""
        code, _ = issue_pairing_code()
        
        # 3 digits
        with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError):
            consume_pairing_code("123", "192.168.1.50")
        
        # 5 digits
        with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError):
            consume_pairing_code("12345", "192.168.1.50")
            
        # Non-numeric
        with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError):
            consume_pairing_code("abcd", "192.168.1.50")
        with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError):
            consume_pairing_code("12a4", "192.168.1.50")

    def test_code_is_single_use(self):
        """Verify single-use behavior."""
        code, expiry = issue_pairing_code()
        self.assertEqual(expiry, 300)
        consume_pairing_code(code, "192.168.1.20")
        with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError):
            consume_pairing_code(code, "192.168.1.20")

    def test_code_expiry(self):
        """Verify code expires after TTL."""
        import dispatch.sync.pairing_codes as pc
        code, _ = issue_pairing_code()
        # Simulate time passing past TTL
        with patch("time.monotonic", return_value=pc._active_code_expires_at + 1):
            with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError) as ctx:
                consume_pairing_code(code, "192.168.1.20")
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status_code, 401)

    def test_lockout_protection_after_five_failed_attempts(self):
        """Verify IP lockout after 5 consecutive invalid attempts."""
        code, _ = issue_pairing_code()
        client_ip = "192.168.1.99"
        
        # 4 failed attempts
        for _ in range(4):
            with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError) as ctx:
                consume_pairing_code("0000" if code != "0000" else "9999", client_ip)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status_code, 401)
            
        # 5th failed attempt triggers lockout
        with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError) as ctx:
            consume_pairing_code("0000" if code != "0000" else "9999", client_ip)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status_code, 401)
        
        # Subsequent attempt (even with valid code!) is locked out with 429
        with self.assertRaises(PairingCodeError) as ctx:
            consume_pairing_code(code, client_ip)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status_code, 429)
        self.assertIn("Too many incorrect pairing attempts", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_complete_pc_generation_to_phone_pairing_flow(self):
        """REMOVED-FLOW CONTRACT (2026-10-24 pivot): PC->phone credential pairing no
        longer exists; on-device OAuth replaces it. Both routes fail closed with 410
        and NEVER return credential material under any input."""
        from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
        from dispatch.web.app import app
        client = TestClient(app)
        pc_resp = client.post(
            "/api/integrations/youtube/pairing-code",
            json={"understands_http_risk": True},
            headers={"host": "localhost:8000"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(pc_resp.status_code, 410)
        phone_resp = client.post(
            "/api/youtube/credentials",
            json={"pairing_code": "1234"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(phone_resp.status_code, 410)
        for body in (pc_resp.text, phone_resp.text):
            for marker in ("refresh_token", "client_secret", "mock-refresh-token"):
                self.assertNotIn(marker, body)

"""Acceptance Test Suite for YouTube Caption Timing & Karaoke Grouping.
Validates:
1. Word-timed VTT preserves real word boundaries through export.
2. Phrase-only VTT does not produce fabricated exact word timings.
3. Three-word caption grouping does not alter source timestamps.
4. Clip trimming does not introduce a constant timing offset.
5. Preview and rendered output stay synchronized.
6. Missing YouTube captions never trigger local Whisper.
7. Existing caption editing and Apply to All styling continue to work.
"""
import unittest
import tempfile
import json
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta

from dispatch.youtube_inbox.vtt_parser import parse_vtt_content
from dispatch.captions.model import CaptionTrack, CaptionGroup, Word, StyleConfig, LayoutConfig, AnimationConfig
from dispatch.captions.grouper import group_words_into_captions
from dispatch.captions.exporter import export_to_ass
from dispatch.transcription.worker import TranscriptionWorker
from dispatch.youtube_inbox.catcher import YouTubeInboxCatcher
from dispatch import db


class TestYouTubeCaptionTimingFix(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        # Configure test database in-memory or isolated
        pass

    def test_1_word_timed_vtt_preserves_real_word_boundaries_through_export(self):
        """1. Word-timed VTT preserves the real word boundaries through export."""
        vtt_content = """WEBVTT

00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:03.500
<00:00:01.000><c> Hello</c><00:00:01.500><c> world</c><00:00:02.000><c> welcome</c>
"""
        segments = parse_vtt_content(vtt_content)
        self.assertEqual(len(segments), 1)
        seg = segments[0]
        self.assertTrue(seg.get("has_word_timestamps"))
        self.assertEqual(len(seg["words"]), 3)

        # Check real boundaries from VTT tags
        w0 = seg["words"][0]
        w1 = seg["words"][1]
        w2 = seg["words"][2]

        self.assertEqual(w0["word"], "Hello")
        self.assertEqual(w0["start"], 1.000)
        self.assertEqual(w0["end"], 1.500)
        self.assertTrue(w0["is_exact"])

        self.assertEqual(w1["word"], "world")
        self.assertEqual(w1["start"], 1.500)
        self.assertEqual(w1["end"], 2.000)
        self.assertTrue(w1["is_exact"])

        self.assertEqual(w2["word"], "welcome")
        self.assertEqual(w2["start"], 2.000)
        self.assertEqual(w2["end"], 3.500)
        self.assertTrue(w2["is_exact"])

        # Group words into captions
        track = group_words_into_captions(segments, clip_start=0.0, clip_end=5.0)
        self.assertEqual(len(track.groups), 1)
        grp = track.groups[0]
        self.assertTrue(grp.has_word_timing)
        self.assertEqual(grp.timing_mode, "word")

        # Export to ASS
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            ass_path = Path(tmpdir) / "test.ass"
            export_to_ass(track, ass_path)
            content = ass_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

            # Dialogue events must reflect authentic word boundaries:
            # Word 0: 1.00s -> 1.50s (0:00:01.00 -> 0:00:01.50)
            self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,0:00:01.00,0:00:01.50", content)
            # Word 1: 1.50s -> 2.00s (0:00:01.50 -> 0:00:02.00)
            self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,0:00:01.50,0:00:02.00", content)
            # Word 2: 2.00s -> 3.50s (0:00:02.00 -> 0:00:03.50)
            self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,0:00:02.00,0:00:03.50", content)

    def test_2_phrase_only_vtt_does_not_produce_fabricated_exact_word_timings(self):
        """2. Phrase-only VTT does not produce fabricated exact word timings."""
        vtt_content = """WEBVTT

00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:04.000
This is a standard YouTube manual caption.
"""
        segments = parse_vtt_content(vtt_content)
        self.assertEqual(len(segments), 1)
        seg = segments[0]
        # Must NOT be marked as having authentic word timestamps
        self.assertFalse(seg.get("has_word_timestamps"))

        # Words must have is_exact=False and NOT have divided progressive timestamps
        words = seg["words"]
        for w in words:
            self.assertFalse(w["is_exact"])
            # Duration must not be linearly divided (e.g. 1.0 -> 1.57, 1.57 -> 2.14)
            self.assertEqual(w["start"], 1.000)
            self.assertEqual(w["end"], 4.000)

        # Group words into captions
        track = group_words_into_captions(segments, clip_start=0.0, clip_end=5.0)
        self.assertEqual(len(track.groups), 1)
        grp = track.groups[0]
        self.assertFalse(grp.has_word_timing)
        self.assertEqual(grp.timing_mode, "phrase")

        # Export to ASS must render as single phrase dialogue without karaoke flashing
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            ass_path = Path(tmpdir) / "phrase.ass"
            export_to_ass(track, ass_path)
            content = ass_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            dialogue_lines = [l for l in content.splitlines() if l.startswith("Dialogue:")]
            # Exactly 1 dialogue event for the phrase, not 7 events for each word
            self.assertEqual(len(dialogue_lines), 1)
            self.assertIn("0:00:01.00,0:00:04.00", dialogue_lines[0])
            # ASS uses \N as an explicit visual line break; normalize it when
            # asserting that phrase-mode text is preserved in one dialogue event.
            dialogue_text = dialogue_lines[0].replace(r"\N", " ")
            self.assertIn("THIS IS A STANDARD YOUTUBE MANUAL CAPTION.", dialogue_text)

    def test_3_three_word_caption_grouping_does_not_alter_source_timestamps(self):
        """3. Three-word caption grouping does not alter source timestamps."""
        raw_segments = [
            {
                "start": 1.0,
                "end": 2.1,
                "words": [
                    {"word": "One", "start": 1.000, "end": 1.300, "is_exact": True},
                    {"word": "Two", "start": 1.400, "end": 1.700, "is_exact": True},
                    {"word": "Three", "start": 1.800, "end": 2.100, "is_exact": True},
                ]
            },
            {
                "start": 2.25,
                "end": 3.0,
                "words": [
                    {"word": "Next", "start": 2.250, "end": 2.800, "is_exact": True}
                ]
            }
        ]

        # Group into captions (gap between 2.100 and 2.250 is 0.15s < 0.25s, so card end will stretch)
        track = group_words_into_captions(raw_segments, clip_start=0.0, clip_end=5.0, words_per_group=3)
        self.assertEqual(len(track.groups), 2)

        grp0 = track.groups[0]
        # Card end was stretched to 2.25 to prevent visual gap flicker
        self.assertEqual(grp0.end, 2.250)

        # BUT the 3rd word's authentic source timestamp MUST remain untouched!
        w_last = grp0.words[2]
        self.assertEqual(w_last.text, "Three")
        self.assertEqual(w_last.start, 1.800)
        self.assertEqual(w_last.end, 2.100, "Source word timestamp must NOT be mutated by gap closure!")

    def test_4_clip_trimming_does_not_introduce_constant_timing_offset(self):
        """4. Clip trimming does not introduce a constant timing offset."""
        # Absolute source video timestamps: 45.0s to 50.0s
        raw_segments = [
            {
                "start": 45.0,
                "end": 47.0,
                "words": [
                    {"word": "Highlight", "start": 45.200, "end": 45.800, "is_exact": True},
                    {"word": "moment", "start": 46.000, "end": 46.700, "is_exact": True}
                ]
            }
        ]

        # Clip trimmed with clip_start=40.0s
        track = group_words_into_captions(raw_segments, clip_start=40.0, clip_end=55.0)
        self.assertEqual(len(track.groups), 1)
        w0 = track.groups[0].words[0]
        w1 = track.groups[0].words[1]

        # Converted to clip-relative time exactly once: 45.2 - 40.0 = 5.2s
        self.assertAlmostEqual(w0.start, 5.200, places=3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(w0.end, 5.800, places=3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(w1.start, 6.000, places=3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(w1.end, 6.700, places=3)

        # Check rolling cue deduplication does not introduce constant offset
        rolling_vtt = """WEBVTT

00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:03.000
First line

00:00:02.000 --> 00:00:04.500
First line second line
"""
        deduped = parse_vtt_content(rolling_vtt)
        self.assertEqual(len(deduped), 2)
        # First cue ends at 3.000s
        self.assertEqual(deduped[0]["end"], 3.000)
        # Second deduped cue "second line" must start at 3.000s, NOT at 2.000s (which would be 1.0s too early!)
        self.assertEqual(deduped[1]["text"], "second line")
        self.assertEqual(deduped[1]["start"], 3.000)

    def test_5_preview_and_rendered_output_stay_synchronized(self):
        """5. Preview and rendered output stay synchronized."""
        raw_segments = [
            {
                "start": 10.0,
                "end": 12.0,
                "words": [
                    {"word": "Sync", "start": 10.200, "end": 10.600, "is_exact": True},
                    {"word": "test", "start": 10.700, "end": 11.200, "is_exact": True}
                ]
            }
        ]
        track = group_words_into_captions(raw_segments, clip_start=10.0, clip_end=15.0)
        w0 = track.groups[0].words[0]
        w1 = track.groups[0].words[1]

        # Frontend preview uses currentTime >= w.start && currentTime <= w.end
        # Preview active window for w0: [0.200, 0.600]
        # Preview active window for w1: [0.700, 1.200]
        self.assertEqual(w0.start, 0.200)
        self.assertEqual(w0.end, 0.600)
        self.assertEqual(w1.start, 0.700)
        self.assertEqual(w1.end, 1.200)

        # Exported ASS must have exact same timecodes
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            ass_path = Path(tmpdir) / "sync.ass"
            export_to_ass(track, ass_path)
            content = ass_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

            # Dialogue for w0 active illumination: 0:00:00.20 to 0:00:00.60
            self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,0:00:00.20,0:00:00.60", content)
            # Dialogue for w1 active illumination: 0:00:00.70 to 0:00:01.20
            self.assertIn("Dialogue: 0,0:00:00.70,0:00:01.20", content)

    def test_6_missing_youtube_captions_never_trigger_local_whisper(self):
        """6. Missing YouTube captions never trigger local Whisper."""
        video_id = "test_no_whisper_yt"
        db.register_youtube_video(video_id=video_id, title="No Whisper Video", duration=120.0)
        past_deadline = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=10)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        db.update_youtube_video(
            video_id=video_id,
            status="WAITING_FOR_TRANSCRIPT",
            transcript_wait_deadline=past_deadline
        )

        mock_catcher = MagicMock()
        mock_catcher.fetch_youtube_captions.return_value = None

        with patch("dispatch.transcription.worker.transcribe_video") as mock_whisper:
            worker = TranscriptionWorker(caption_wait_seconds=60, catcher=mock_catcher)
            res = worker.process_pending()

            # Whisper must NEVER be invoked!
            mock_whisper.assert_not_called()

            # Result must be CAPTIONS_UNAVAILABLE
            self.assertEqual(len(res), 1)
            self.assertEqual(res[0]["status"], "CAPTIONS_UNAVAILABLE")

        # Database record must reflect CAPTIONS_UNAVAILABLE
        yt_rec = db.get_youtube_video(video_id)
        self.assertEqual(yt_rec["status"], "CAPTIONS_UNAVAILABLE")
        self.assertIn("unavailable", yt_rec["last_error"].lower())

    def test_7_existing_caption_editing_and_apply_to_all_styling_continue_to_work(self):
        """7. Existing caption editing and Apply to All styling continue to work."""
        # Build multi-group track
        g1 = CaptionGroup(
            id="grp_1",
            start=0.0,
            end=2.0,
            words=[Word(id="w1", text="First", start=0.0, end=1.0), Word(id="w2", text="card", start=1.0, end=2.0)],
            style=StyleConfig(font_family="Impact", font_size=54, primary_color="#FFFFFF")
        )
        g2 = CaptionGroup(
            id="grp_2",
            start=2.5,
            end=4.5,
            words=[Word(id="w3", text="Second", start=2.5, end=3.5), Word(id="w4", text="card", start=3.5, end=4.5)],
            style=StyleConfig(font_family="Roboto", font_size=42, primary_color="#00FF00")
        )
        track = CaptionTrack(clip_id="clip_apply_all", groups=[g1, g2])

        # Test JSON round-trip
        data = track.to_dict()
        reconstituted = CaptionTrack.from_dict(data)

        self.assertEqual(len(reconstituted.groups), 2)
        self.assertEqual(reconstituted.groups[0].style.font_family, "Impact")
        self.assertEqual(reconstituted.groups[1].style.font_family, "Roboto")
        self.assertTrue(reconstituted.groups[0].has_word_timing)

        # Simulate editing caption text
        reconstituted.groups[0].words[0].text = "EditedFirst"
        self.assertEqual(reconstituted.groups[0].words[0].text, "EditedFirst")

        # Export to ASS works with custom styles
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            ass_path = Path(tmpdir) / "edited.ass"
            export_to_ass(reconstituted, ass_path)
            content = ass_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIn("EDITEDFIRST", content)
            self.assertIn("SECOND", content)
