Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HE4rLEQpiXY
Title: How to think like a GENIUS UI/UX designer

Most designers want to work for big tech or start an agency, but most designers want, most designers focus on making things look good, but genius designers don't. They focus on making things work brilliantly for the user. Think of web design not as art, but as a story, and that every story needs 3D graphics or battery spin scrolling. If your goal is to impress other designers, maybe. But if your goal is to guide someone to an action, all that flare might just be in the way.

Start with user intent. Let's say you need to design a user flow that enables customers to rent vacation properties, not unlike Airbnb. A UI designer might start thinking about the icons or the layout of each card, and entirely lose the plot of why we're designing. The intent of the user is to search for accommodations. So, a search bar is a natural starting point. We can then augment with useful features like destination, amount of travelers and dates.

You might think the next step is to put a header above this and slap an image on the background. But think about the user. Does this design do anything extra that this design didn't? Not at all, but there can be more than one intent for a website. Maybe the user knows they want to go on a vacation, but doesn't know where. They're there to browse. We can serve that intent too by displaying our listings.

But the user probably wants something more specific, so we can add in filtering UI elements. Notice how the fonts, colors and icons affect the aesthetics, but do very little to change the functionality. Only as the user intent expands do we expand the functionality of our designs. But we jump the gun a little by building full UI's before talking about leveraging existing layouts. Why not put the search bar down here or arrange the cards like this?

Should be told, nothing is stopping us from making UI like this. If it serves the user better. But after 30 plus years of websites, users have come to expect certain layouts. This doesn't preclude us from trying new layouts, but means that typically information should flow top to bottom and left to right. Navigation is at the top of the page, and call the actions are typically eye catching and easy to find.

Designs that follow these guides are generally much easier to integrate new sections seamlessly and make responsive. Respecting these expectations, but making the design uniquely yours, like adding a cool micro-interaction or a set of unique features is what separates the good from the genius. And if you're trying to think like a genius designer, it helps to see how the best are already thinking. Mobbin is a curated library of real-world UI and UX, from full user flows down to individual components, all pulled from top apps and websites.

Instead of downloading dozens of apps just to reverse engineer their design patterns, Mobbin lets you search and explore them all in one place. Personally, I'm always diving into the UI element section. With a link in the description, if you do want to check it out, thank you Mobbin for sponsoring this video. But without a content structure, design has very little value. There are two steps to designing around content.

The first is to decide which content to display. Understanding how the user will interact with the design will determine what type of information is presented. For example, on our travel page, we can include a short description for every listing, but if the user wants a detailed look, they'll just click on the listing. They need the specifics to scan, like the location, rating and price before anything else.

The second step is structuring the content that we do display. Currently, our design has perfect content, meaning that the titles and locations are all short. But what if we had a destination with a really long name or save icons on really bright listing images? We would probably want to truncate long names and add a circle to the icon to guarantee contrast. Otherwise, you end up with unintended consequences which are not fun to deal with.

Animations should add clarity or functionality to a design. Just take a look at my old portfolio website. It's awful. All of these animations didn't do anything. Navigation is a great example of this. As we add more links, we simply run out of room, so we can solidate them into a menu that can animate in, serving a purpose. Or if our web app starts to take on a browsing priority, instead of sticking this block to the top of the screen, we can reduce the size of the search bar and have it animate in when clicked.

These are all great examples of progressive disclosure, showing the user what they need to see and revealing more as it's required. That's why a load more button is preferable over infinite scroll. It gives the user more control and, crucially, it lets them actually breach the footer. Something infinite scroll often makes impossible. Context matters, but as a general rule, buttons should almost always have a small animation, while scroll jacking effects should be used very sparingly if ever.

Finally, design systems add a layer of replicability and speed that's tough to match. But the system has to reflect the values of the team. A lean startup might need something lightweight and flexible, quick to update, and easy to scrap, whereas something like Google's Material Design is massive and deeply defined because the use cases span dozens of products and billions of users. More importantly, the development of a design system is often more critical than the design itself.

The process of defining rules, spacing, typography scales, interaction patterns gives you an architecture for expansion. But a design system isn't about making everything look the same. It's about giving your team a shared language. And like any language, mastery means knowing when to bend the rules. You don't break this system by accident, you break it with intention. Overall, I hope this gave some perspective on how to think like a better designer.

If you're interested in checking out Robin, it'll be the first link in the description below. And thanks for watching.

def format_into_paragraphs(text, target_words=70):
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text)
    paragraphs = []
    current_para = []
    current_count = 0
    for s in sentences:
        s = s.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        current_para.append(s)
        current_count += len(s.split())
        if current_count >= target_words:
            paragraphs.append(" ".join(current_para))
            current_para = []
            current_count = 0
    if current_para:
        paragraphs.append(" ".join(current_para))
    return "\n\n".join(paragraphs)

def main():
    print("Loading faster_whisper base model...")
    model = WhisperModel("base", device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
    print("Model loaded successfully.\n")

    for item in MISSING_VIDEOS:
        idx = item["index"]
        vid = item["video_id"]
        url = item["url"]
        title = item["title"]
        filename = item["filename"]
        out_path = os.path.join(TRANSCRIPT_DIR, filename)

        print(f"=== Processing [{idx}/18] {vid}: {title} ===")
        audio_pattern = os.path.join(TRANSCRIPT_DIR, f"temp_{vid}.*")

        # 1. Download audio stream
        print(f"  Downloading audio stream for {vid} via yt-dlp...")
        cmd = [
            "yt-dlp",
            "-f", "bestaudio",
            f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}",
            "-o", os.path.join(TRANSCRIPT_DIR, f"temp_{vid}.%(ext)s")
        ]
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

        # Locate downloaded audio file
        matches = glob.glob(audio_pattern)
        if not matches:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Audio file for {vid} not found")
        audio_file = matches[0]

        # 2. Transcribe audio with Whisper
        print(f"  Transcribing {os.path.basename(audio_file)} with faster_whisper...")
        segments, info = model.transcribe(audio_file, beam_size=5)
        raw_text_parts = [s.text.strip() for s in segments if s.text.strip()]
        full_raw_text = " ".join(raw_text_parts)
        formatted_transcript = format_into_paragraphs(full_raw_text)

        word_count = len(formatted_transcript.split())
        print(f"  Done! Words transcribed: {word_count}")

        # 3. Clean up audio file
        try:
            os.remove(audio_file)
        except Exception:
            pass

        # 4. Save individual file
        file_content = (
            f"Link: {url}\n"
            f"Title: {title}\n\n"
            f"{formatted_transcript}\n"
        )
        with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(file_content)
        print(f"  Saved: {filename}")

        # Delay between items as requested
        print("  Waiting 4s before next video...\n")
        time.sleep(4)

    # 5. Rebuild Combined_Transcripts.txt from all 18 files
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("Rebuilding Combined_Transcripts.txt from all 18 files in order...")
    
    # Collect all files 01_*.txt through 18_*.txt
    all_files = []
    for f in os.listdir(TRANSCRIPT_DIR):
        m = re.match(r"^(\d{2})_.*\.txt$", f)
        if m:
            all_files.append((int(m.group(1)), f))

    all_files.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    print(f"Found {len(all_files)} files: {[x[1] for x in all_files]}")

    combined_blocks = []
    for file_idx, f_name in all_files:
        f_path = os.path.join(TRANSCRIPT_DIR, f_name)
        with open(f_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            content = f.read().strip()
            combined_blocks.append(content)

    combined_text = "\n\n\n\n\n".join(combined_blocks) + "\n"
    combined_path = os.path.join(TRANSCRIPT_DIR, "Combined_Transcripts.txt")
    with open(combined_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(combined_text)

    print(f"Successfully generated {combined_path}!")
    print(f"Total combined entries: {len(combined_blocks)}")
    print("=" * 60)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

OUTPUT_DIR = r"C:\CODE\Dispatch\Transcript"
INTER_REQUEST_DELAY = 4  # Seconds to wait between videos

_WHISPER_MODEL = None


def get_video_id(url):
    m = re.search(r"v=([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)", url)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def get_api_key():
    for attempt in range(2):
        try:
            r = requests.get("https://youtube2text.org/api/demo-key", timeout=10)
            if r.status_code == 200:
                data = r.json()
                key = data.get("apiKey")
                if key:
                    return key
        except Exception as e:
            time.sleep(1)
    return None


def fetch_oembed_title(vid):
    try:
        url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
        oembed_url = f"https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url={url}&format=json"
        req = urllib.request.Request(oembed_url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
            data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            return data.get("title")
    except Exception:
        return None


def format_into_paragraphs(text, target_words=70):
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    # Clean replacement characters
    text = text.replace("\ufffd", "'")
    sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text)
    words = text.split()

    # If text has few/no sentence delimiters (common in auto captions), chunk words directly
    if len(sentences) <= 3 and len(words) > 100:
        paragraphs = []
        for i in range(0, len(words), target_words):
            chunk = " ".join(words[i : i + target_words])
            paragraphs.append(chunk)
        return "\n\n".join(paragraphs)

    paragraphs = []
    current_para = []
    current_count = 0
    for s in sentences:
        s = s.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        current_para.append(s)
        current_count += len(s.split())
        if current_count >= target_words:
            paragraphs.append(" ".join(current_para))
            current_para = []
            current_count = 0
    if current_para:
        paragraphs.append(" ".join(current_para))
    return "\n\n".join(paragraphs)


def sanitize_filename(name):
    clean = re.sub(r'[\\/*?:"<>|]', "", name)
    clean = clean.strip().replace(" ", "_")
    return clean[:90]


def find_existing_transcript_on_disk(idx):
    prefix = f"{idx:02d}_"
    for fname in os.listdir(OUTPUT_DIR):
        if fname.startswith(prefix) and fname.endswith(".txt"):
            fpath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, fname)
            try:
                with open(fpath, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                parts = content.split("\n\n", 1)
                body = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else content.strip()
                if body and "[Transcript could not be retrieved]" not in body and len(body.split()) > 30:
                    return body
            except Exception:
                pass
    return None


def get_whisper_model():
    global _WHISPER_MODEL
    if _WHISPER_MODEL is None:
        print("  [Whisper] Loading faster_whisper base model (CPU)...")
        from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
        _WHISPER_MODEL = WhisperModel("base", device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
        print("  [Whisper] Model loaded successfully.")
    return _WHISPER_MODEL


def transcribe_via_whisper(vid):
    audio_pattern = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f"temp_{vid}.*")
    # Clean any stale temp files first
    for f in glob.glob(audio_pattern):
        try:
            os.remove(f)
        except Exception:
            pass

    out_tmpl = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f"temp_{vid}.%(ext)s")
    print(f"  [Whisper] Downloading audio stream with yt-dlp for {vid}...")
    cmd = [
        "yt-dlp",
        "-f", "bestaudio",
        f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}",
        "-o", out_tmpl
    ]
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    matches = glob.glob(audio_pattern)
    if not matches:
        print(f"  [Whisper] Could not find downloaded audio file for {vid}.")
        return None

    audio_file = matches[0]
    try:
        model = get_whisper_model()
        print(f"  [Whisper] Transcribing {os.path.basename(audio_file)}...")
        segments, _ = model.transcribe(audio_file, beam_size=5)
        raw_text_parts = [s.text.strip() for s in segments if s.text.strip()]
        return " ".join(raw_text_parts)
    finally:
        # Clean up temp audio file
        try:
            if os.path.exists(audio_file):
                os.remove(audio_file)
        except Exception:
            pass


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    print("=" * 70)
    print(" " * 15 + "DISPATCH TRANSCRIPT FETCHER")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Total videos to process : {len(URLS)}")
    print(f"Destination directory   : {OUTPUT_DIR}")
    print(f"Inter-video delay       : {INTER_REQUEST_DELAY} seconds\n")

    api_key = get_api_key()
    if api_key:
        print("Online demo API key acquired for fast retrieval.")
    else:
        print("Online demo API key unavailable. Fallback mechanisms active.")

    cache = {}  # vid -> {"title": ..., "transcript": ...}
    results = []

    for idx, url in enumerate(URLS, 1):
        vid = get_video_id(url)
        print(f"\n--- [{idx:02d}/{len(URLS):02d}] Video ID: {vid} ---")
        print(f"URL: {url}")

        # Determine canonical title
        title = CANONICAL_TITLES.get(idx) or fetch_oembed_title(vid) or f"YouTube Video {vid}"

        transcript_text = None
        source = None

        # 1. Check in-memory cache for duplicate video IDs (e.g. video 2 & 15)
        if vid in cache and cache[vid]["transcript"]:
            print(f"  Reusing cached transcript from current session ({vid})...")
            transcript_text = cache[vid]["transcript"]
            source = "Session Cache"

        # 2. Check local disk for existing valid transcript
        if not transcript_text:
            disk_transcript = find_existing_transcript_on_disk(idx)
            if disk_transcript:
                print(f"  Loaded existing transcript from disk.")
                transcript_text = format_into_paragraphs(disk_transcript)
                source = "Disk File"

        # 3. Try youtube2text.org API if key is present
        if not transcript_text and api_key:
            print("  Fetching via youtube2text API...")
            try:
                tr_url = f"https://youtube2text.org/api/transcribe?url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
                r = requests.get(tr_url, headers={"x-api-key": api_key}, timeout=35)
                if r.status_code == 200:
                    res = r.json().get("result", {})
                    raw_content = res.get("content", "")
                    if raw_content:
                        transcript_text = format_into_paragraphs(raw_content)
                        source = "youtube2text API"
                elif r.status_code == 429:
                    print("  [youtube2text] Rate limit reached.")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  [youtube2text Error] {e}")

        # 4. Try youtube_transcript_api
        if not transcript_text:
            print("  Attempting youtube_transcript_api...")
            try:
                from youtube_transcript_api import YouTubeTranscriptApi
                ytt_api = YouTubeTranscriptApi()
                snippets = ytt_api.fetch(vid)
                raw_text = " ".join(s.text.replace("\n", " ").strip() for s in snippets)
                if raw_text:
                    transcript_text = format_into_paragraphs(raw_text)
                    source = "youtube_transcript_api"
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  [youtube_transcript_api Failed] {e}")

        # 5. Fallback to yt-dlp + faster_whisper
        if not transcript_text:
            print("  Running local whisper transcription fallback...")
            try:
                raw_text = transcribe_via_whisper(vid)
                if raw_text:
                    transcript_text = format_into_paragraphs(raw_text)
                    source = "yt-dlp + faster_whisper"
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  [Whisper Failed] {e}")

        if not transcript_text:
            transcript_text = "[Transcript could not be retrieved]"
            source = "Failed"

        # Cache for subsequent occurrences
        cache[vid] = {
            "title": title,
            "transcript": transcript_text
        }

        word_count = len(transcript_text.split())
        print(f"Title  : {title}")
        print(f"Source : {source}")
        print(f"Words  : {word_count}")

        # Save individual file
        safe_title = sanitize_filename(title)
        filename = f"{idx:02d}_{safe_title}.txt"
        filepath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, filename)

        individual_content = (
            f"Link: {url}\n"
            f"Title: {title}\n\n"
            f"{transcript_text}\n"
        )

        with open(filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(individual_content)
        print(f"Saved  : {filename}")

        results.append({
            "index": idx,
            "video_id": vid,
            "url": url,
            "title": title,
            "words": word_count,
            "source": source,
            "filename": filename,
            "transcript": transcript_text
        })

        # Inter-request delay between videos to process slowly one by one
        if idx < len(URLS):
            print(f"Waiting {INTER_REQUEST_DELAY}s before next video...")
            time.sleep(INTER_REQUEST_DELAY)

    # Combine all transcripts into Combined_Transcripts.txt with 4 blank lines separation
    combined_blocks = []
    for item in results:
        block = (
            f"Link: {item['url']}\n"
            f"Title: {item['title']}\n\n"
            f"{item['transcript']}"
        )
        combined_blocks.append(block)

    combined_content = "\n\n\n\n\n".join(combined_blocks) + "\n"
    combined_filepath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "Combined_Transcripts.txt")
    with open(combined_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(combined_content)

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print(" " * 22 + "ALL TRANSCRIPTS COMPLETE")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"{'#':<3} | {'Words':<6} | {'Source':<24} | {'Title'}")
    print("-" * 70)
    for item in results:
        t_trunc = item['title'][:35] + ("..." if len(item['title']) > 35 else "")
        print(f"{item['index']:02d}  | {item['words']:<6} | {item['source']:<24} | {t_trunc}")
    print("-" * 70)
    print(f"Combined file saved to: {combined_filepath} ({os.path.getsize(combined_filepath):,} bytes)")
    print("=" * 70)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import os
import re

DIR = r"C:\CODE\Dispatch\Transcript"

# Specific canonical titles and URLs
VIDEO_DATA = {
    1: {"id": "B7k5rOgmOGY", "title": "EVERYTHING you need to know to build a Dashboard UI in 8 minutes (beginner friendly)"},

    12: {"id": "8pMUkEbAM7g", "title": "Top 5 UX/UI Design Tips and Tricks Every Designer Needs to Know About, part 1"},
    13: {"id": "SfX43uIubj4", "title": "4 UI Design Hacks to KILL boring designs"},
    14: {"id": "RCneB_MQ7qs", "title": "The one thing vibe coding CAN'T fix about your website"},
    15: {"id": "Ksx9C2-3yMo", "title": "The 3 dashboard UI flaws that give away you've NEVER built one"},
    16: {"id": "66oOi9OLMCw", "title": "Why the 60-30-10 Rule is 'RUINING' Your UI Designs"},
    17: {"id": "PDcQJOPby1k", "title": "5 SaaS UI/UX mistakes that SCREAM you Vibe Code"},
    18: {"id": "HE4rLEQpiXY", "title": "How to think like a GENIUS UI/UX designer"},
}

# 1. Clean up any obsolete temporary files or small files
for f in os.listdir(DIR):
    if f.startswith("temp_") or f in ["test_api.py", "test_proxy_yt2text.py", "copy_cookies.py"]:
        try:
            os.remove(os.path.join(DIR, f))
        except Exception:
            pass

# 2. Check each individual file and ensure clean Title & Link header
files = []
for f in os.listdir(DIR):
    m = re.match(r"^(\d{2})_.*\.txt$", f)
    if m:
        num = int(m.group(1))
        files.append((num, f))

files.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])

# Deduplicate if duplicate filenames for a number exist (keep largest)
by_num = {}
for num, fname in files:
    fpath = os.path.join(DIR, fname)
    size = os.path.getsize(fpath)
    if num not in by_num or size > by_num[num][1]:
        if num in by_num:
            # remove smaller duplicate
            os.remove(os.path.join(DIR, by_num[num][0]))
        by_num[num] = (fname, size)

final_files = sorted(by_num.items(), key=lambda x: x[0])
print(f"Verified {len(final_files)} unique files for videos 01 to 18.")

combined_blocks = []
stats = []

for num, (fname, size) in final_files:
    fpath = os.path.join(DIR, fname)
    with open(fpath, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        text = f.read()

    # Split header lines and body
    parts = text.split("\n\n", 1)
    if len(parts) == 2:
        header, body = parts
        # Clean any replacement characters from body
        body = body.replace("\ufffd", "'").strip()
    else:
        body = text.replace("\ufffd", "'").strip()

    canonical_title = VIDEO_DATA[num]["title"]
    # Extract url from header or construct
    url_match = re.search(r"Link:\s*(\S+)", text)
    url = url_match.group(1) if url_match else f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={VIDEO_DATA[num]['id']}"

    clean_file_content = f"Link: {url}\nTitle: {canonical_title}\n\n{body}\n"
    with open(fpath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(clean_file_content)

    words = len(body.split())
    stats.append({
        "num": num,
        "filename": fname,
        "url": url,
        "title": canonical_title,
        "words": words,
        "bytes": os.path.getsize(fpath)
    })

    # Combined block format
    combined_block = f"Link: {url}\nTitle: {canonical_title}\n\n{body}"
    combined_blocks.append(combined_block)

# 3. Create Combined_Transcripts.txt with generous space between them as requested:
# "make sure to keep the space in in between them and when you are like. Adding the transcripts, make sure you add the link and the title of that video and below that you will be pasting the transcript and below that there should be some space and again the link, the video title, then the transcript."
separator = "\n\n\n\n\n" + ("=" * 80) + "\n\n\n\n\n"
combined_content = separator.join(combined_blocks) + "\n"

combined_filepath = os.path.join(DIR, "Combined_Transcripts.txt")
with open(combined_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(combined_content)

print(f"\nSaved Combined_Transcripts.txt: {os.path.getsize(combined_filepath):,} bytes")
print("=" * 95)
print(f"{'#':<3} | {'Words':<6} | {'Bytes':<7} | {'Title'}")
print("-" * 95)
for s in stats:
    print(f"{s['num']:02d}  | {s['words']:<6} | {s['bytes']:<7} | {s['title']}")
print("=" * 95)
